Open limits

  • World Bank history is latest-revised, not historical publication vintage; IMF WEO API/workbook access remains locally blocked and is reported as a failure.
  • The 9% WACC and 2.5% terminal growth are transparent scenario inputs, not calibrated conclusions.
  • KB, Itau, and Nu require FCFE or residual-income models; SK Square requires NAV/SOTP rather than corporate FCFF DCF.
  • Kioxia, Sandisk, Qnity, and Arm lack five comparable standalone PIT annual observations because of recent IPO or separation histories.
  • Hyundai's consolidated cash flow includes a material financial-services business, so its FCFF scenario needs segment-level refinement.
  • Component-price history begins with retained public snapshots; free sources do not provide a complete ten-year DRAM/NAND/CPU/GPU PIT backfill.
  • No per-share DCF is decision-ready until shares, net debt, currency, WACC, and price anchors tie out.
  • Exact in-app Browser acceptance remains unrun if the host refuses the canonical Drive file URL.
